# M0-s-02: closing check of consolidation round C1 (lane `check/M0-s-02-consolidate-close-1`, flow flow-7, stage group S, 2026-10-11)

The seat ran in a Claude Code cloud container on 2026-10-11 from 19:07 UTC: Opus 5.5, Linux x64, Node v24.12.0. The
machine check printed `linux:Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz:4cpu:16gib`, which matches the brief, and
`tools/test_budget.py` printed 1 (and `--mutants` 1), so every vitest run used `--maxWorkers=1` and the mutants ran one
at a time. The seat is an implementer-side closing checker. It wrote no part of the item: it is not the author (L-0078),
a fixer (L-0084, L-0441 for this round's `build/M0-s-02-consolidate-1`) or an earlier checker (L-0081, L-0087). Its
ledger row is L-0442 in `CLEAN-ROOM.md` §2.

How the seat worked:

* It changed no file of the item. It wrote this file, rows N6 – N8 of `checks/M0-s-02-notes.md`, its CLEAN-ROOM row,
  its two landed records and its lane-log lines. It ran no git command. The verdict file is `checks/M0-s-02-c1.md`
  (J269); `checks/M0-s-02.md` stays as committed.
* **The before tree, without git.** The round changed files after the last commit, and the builder's before-mirror
  was deleted. The seat fetched the tables package's 49 files read-only through the GitHub contents API (`gh api
  repos/…/contents/<path>?ref=23d13d5`, the session's base commit) and checked each against the wave snapshot
  `landed/snapshots/flow-7.json`: **49 / 49 SHA-256 equal** (the remote's later `main` differs only in the three
  workLimits files, M0-f-03a's). The landed record's `changed` statuses are against that snapshot, so these bytes are
  the tree as it was before the round. `before` = a copy of `plat/` with the item's 15 changed files put back and
  `test/loader/support.ts` removed; `after` = a copy of `plat/` as it stands. Each mirror was installed with
  `--frozen-lockfile --offline` (node_modules and `dist/` excluded, the vendored `simplex-noise/dist` copied back);
  `@plat/*` resolved inside each mirror (`readlink -f`).
  The mirrors (and a third, `mut`, for the mutants) were deleted at the end, node_modules first.
* **Disclosure.** The resume rule's grep of the lane log printed the builder's CHECKPOINT and LANDED lines. The seat
  read C-0323, L-0441 and the builder's old → new map in `checks/M0-s-02-notes.md` only after its own NO-SHIFT probe
  and its first mutant batch had run; its probes and mutants were planned from the plan's §1.1 ORACLE lists, the
  first check's mutant tables and the code. The builder's self-check folders were not opened.

## 1. T-1 – T-3: one grammar, one text predicate, one issue builder

* **T-1** — `cell/cell.ts` `export const STABLE_KEY = /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.\-]*$/` (no flag) replaces `KEY_VALUE`
  (`cell.ts:73` before) and `CELL_KEY` (`table.ts:39` before); the diff shows the three regex texts identical.
  `valueProblem` and `checkTable`'s cell-key test read it; `ROW_KEY` (`/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.\-]*$/`) stays in
  `table.ts` with the comment "a stable key that may also begin with a digit". Imported by path
  (`'../cell/cell.js'`); `cell/index.ts` byte-identical (it lists neither).
* **T-2** — `nonEmptyString` exported from `cell.ts` (same body); `checkTable`'s `section` test calls it, message
  verbatim.
* **T-3** — `issueAt({ table, row, cell, reason })` builds `{ table, reason }` / `{ table, row, reason }` /
  `{ table, row, cell, reason }`, keys in that order, a cell only within its row; `checkTable`'s closure, `checkCell`'s
  closure, `Table.refuse`, `loadTable`, `View.table` and `ladder.ts`'s four sites build through it. The bare literals
  and three-way conditionals the plan lists are gone (`grep -rn "{ table:" src/loader src/cell` outside `issueAt` calls finds only a `SliceRef` and a `CellAt`, neither an issue).
* **Oracle:** `cell.test.ts`, `loader.test.ts`, `ladder.test.ts` whole green (NEAR, below); every refusal's `issues`
  JSON, `Object.keys` per issue, `message`, `table/row/cell/reason` and the `issues` freeze **byte-identical** before vs
  after over the NO-SHIFT corpus (8 230 `TableError` captures, §6). New pin "builds each issue with its keys in order,
  an absent key left absent, never undefined" kills N01 – N04, N27, N28, N30. Mutants (§7): N05, N06, N08 (grammar),
  N09, N10, N32 (text predicate), N01 – N04, N25, N27 – N31 (issue shapes and sites) all red; the plan's named
  M01 – M05, M12 – M14, M18 – M20, M22, S04, S06, S08, S10 – S13 red.

## 3. T-5, T-6: the vocabularies and the ids written once, the types identical

* `unit.ts`: one private `UNIT_WORDS = [...] as const`, `export type Unit = (typeof UNIT_WORDS)[number]`,
  `export const UNITS: readonly Unit[] = Object.freeze(UNIT_WORDS)`. `cell.ts`: private `EXTENSION_OVERS`,
  `EXTENSION_MODES`, `PRESET_IDS` (`as const`), the three types derived, the sets built from them. `REFERENCES` kept
  apart (T-5 (c)), its comment naming the three vocabularies. `registry.ts`: `TABLE_IDS` the one `as const` list,
  `JSON_OF: Readonly<Record<M0TableId, unknown>>`, `TABLE_SOURCES = new Map(TABLE_IDS.map(...))`, no cast.
* **Types (J268 Q6), CONFIRMED by the compiler:** a scratch file in the after mirror imported both trees' barrels
  (`import type * as N` / `* as O`) and asserted exact type equality (`<T>() => T extends A ? 1 : 2` form) for 29 pairs:
  `Unit`, `ExtensionOver`, `ExtensionMode`, `PresetId`, `typeof UNITS`, `typeof TABLE_IDS`, `M0TableId`,
  `typeof TABLE_SOURCES`, `TableIssue`, `Cell`, `CellAt`, `CellValue`, `PresetValue`, `ProvenanceForm`, `RungProfile`,
  `Row`, `typeof BASE_RUNGS`, the signatures of `checkCell`, `isUnit`, `checkTable`, `isTableId`, `calibratableCensus`,
  `REFERENCES`, `isRecord`, `cellPinning`, `rowPinning`, `provenanceForm`, `minCorridorM`, and `keyof typeof` the barrel
  (every value export name). `tsc` reported exactly the two planted inequalities and nothing else.
* **Exports:** `cell/index.ts`, `loader/index.ts` and `src/index.ts`'s export lines byte-identical to the before tree
  (`src/index.ts` differs only in its two comment lines, the RS change, which is M0-s-01's file and in no record of this
  item); the runtime export lists of the barrel and of the cell, loader and workLimits indexes (name and `typeof`)
  identical in the probe. `tsc -b` green (gate). The new type pins "derives the Unit type from the list" and "types the
  markers with §7.6's words" turn `tsc -b` red under N20, N22, N23, N24.
* Mutants N17 (two JSON sources swapped), N18 (map order), N19 (id order), N20 – N24 red. **Nuance kept:** `TABLE_IDS`
  is not frozen at runtime, before or after (probe `TABLE_IDS.frozen` false on both) — the plan's "Object.freeze … as

## 6. NO-SHIFT

A probe (`tsx --conditions=plat-source`, run against each mirror's own `src/index.ts`) wrote 17 091 lines per tree:
the export lists of the barrel and the three indexes; `UNITS`, `REFERENCES`, `TABLE_IDS` and their freeze; each
source's hash; every table's id, version, section, hash and freeze; every row's hash, pinning content, row slice and
`view.get`; every cell's JSON (key order included), own keys, freeze, pinning content, field slice, `has` and each of
the seven typed accessors (value or refusal); missing-row and missing-cell refusals per row and table; `checkTable`
of each source; the view hashes over 26 id subsets and orders and its three refusals; `calibratableCensus` (default,
subset, empty, unknown); `minCorridorM`; `rungProfile` for seven rung words and a non-ladder table;
`rungForPopulation` at eleven populations; `loadWorkLimits` and `workLimitsCensus`; a malformed corpus of 6 731
mutations of the shipped tables (39 cell mutations on a sample of cells of every table — missing fields, empty and
prose values, bad units and provenances, bad markers and presets, categorical options — plus row-key, cell-key and
top-level mutations and non-object files; each as `parseTable`'s hash or its refusal, and `checkTable`'s full issue
list); a ladder sweep (13 values into every cell of the three base rows, and each cell deleted); and `checkCell`
directly. Result: **byte-identical** (sha256 `2ed498dc…` both trees; 8 230 `TableError` captures with message,
`issues` JSON, per-issue keys and freeze). The fourteen data files, `golden.json`, `calibratable-census.json`,
`extension-cells.json` and `string-values.json` are byte-identical to the snapshot. A second probe of the keys
`a/b`, `a/`, `a b`, `a,b`, `#f00`, `é`, `a\n` as cell key, key value and row key: identical on both trees.

**Refusals of lawful input (J264), re-measured:** the 13 shipped tables load (`checkTable` empty ×13), the 3 base rung
profiles read, 471 lawful slices hash, the two fast-check properties and the simulated hand-overs of `tables.test.ts`
green — **0 before, 0 after** (not risen). **Exit bar** (every cell carries unit, provenance and calibratable; the
counter-examples refused): 396 / 396 delete-a-field counter-examples refused naming the table, the row and the cell
with `lacks …`, on both trees.

round's promise is "the grammar written once, every acceptance and refusal unchanged": the regex text is identical
before and after (diff), the slash probe is identical on both trees, and the same widening of `KEY_VALUE` and
`CELL_KEY` survives the BEFORE sources with the BEFORE tests (246 / 246) — the gap is older than the round and nothing
reads wrongly (a cell key with `/` would still slice correctly at the first `/`). Under N-45/J202 a further hardening
test is a note: **N6** (one new `it` refusing `a/b` as a cell key and a key value; M4). Mutant count: 58 is above the
"about forty" guide because the plan's oracles name some 30 earlier mutants on top of the round's own lines; each is
